title: Reflect then Translate: y = -f(x) + 1
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Describe the two-step transformation producing y=-f(x)+1 from y=f(x), and give the image of a point (a,b). Explain why the order of operations matters.
finalAnswer: (a,b)\mapsto(a,1-b):\ \text{reflect across the } x\text{-axis, then shift up } 1

steps.title: Step One: Negate
steps.explanation: First flip the graph across the x-axis, sending (a,b) to (a,-b).
steps.why: The negation binds to f(x) itself, i.e. to the output before anything is added.

steps.title: Step Two: Raise
steps.explanation: Then shift the flipped graph up one unit, sending (a,-b) to (a,-b+1)=(a,1-b).
steps.why: Adding 1 outside acts after the reflection on every height.

steps.title: Compare Reversed Orders
steps.explanation: Shifting up first and reflecting second would yield -f(x)-1, a different graph, so the reading order (reflect, then raise) is essential.
steps.why: Reflection negates whatever has been built so far, including any earlier vertical shift.

steps.title: Describe the Sketch
steps.explanation: The curve hangs as a mirror image below/above the line y=1/2 relative to the original: heights b become 1-b, and points at height b=1/2 are fixed.
steps.why: The map b -> 1-b is reflection across the horizontal line y=1/2.
